tells: 1. Faces carry an unmotivated frontal key: the only practicals are tealight candles and wall sconces, yet every front-row face is evenly lit from camera side with no candle under-light or falloff, so the crowd reads as composited onto the room (club-1-wide.png, front row centre; club-3-mid.png, centre faces)
2. Close-up skin is waxy and uniform with flat, glassy eyes and a wide-lens stretched jaw; reads as game cutscene, not a person (club-4-face.png, centre face and neck)
3. Wide shot front row is posed like a catalogue: near-identical forearms-on-table, everyone facing the same direction, symmetrical spacing at round tables (club-1-wide.png, lower half centre)

4. Back of the room is grey standing silhouettes with no seats or tables under them, and the bar backlight panel is a flat cutout with a figure pasted in front (club-1-wide.png, upper middle and bar at right of centre; club-2-mid.png, upper left)

5. Laugh onset is legible but the front-row reactions start within one 0.2 s step of each other and hand gestures (clasped hands at chest) repeat across neighbours (club-5-strip.png, frames t=12.6 to 13.0, centre group)

1. Rows behind the front two read as people standing or floating, not seated in raked seats: torsos and legs visible, seat backs absent, figures in the aisle at the far left (theatre-1-wide.png, left third and rows 3-6; theatre-6-held.png, same)

2. Exposure is a hard spotlight pool on rows 0-1 that dies abruptly; the rest of the house is murky grey-blue with no haze shafts or stage spill gradient, so depth reads as a cut-off rather than a falling light (theatre-1-wide.png, mid frame boundary at row 2)

3. Close-up has porcelain specular skin, overlong fingers curled unnaturally against the cheek, flat cap-like hair and blocky out-of-focus red seats behind (theatre-4-face.png, centre hand and face, lower corners)
4. Slumped figures with heads dropped onto the chest look asleep or broken, at odds with a laughing row (theatre-3-mid.png, far right man in cap; theatre-6-held.png, teal hoodie centre front)

5. Laugh arrives late and in a block: nothing until t=12.6, then four front-row mouths open in the same 0.2 s step with near-identical open-jaw shapes (theatre-5-strip.png, frames t=12.8 and 13.0, front row)

1. Hair cards break up: noisy dithered strands at the crown and a torn floating patch on top of the afro, very visible at TV distance (openmic-4-face.png, top right of the head; openmic-6-held.png, centre-right afro top; openmic-2-mid.png, afro crown)

2. Lighting is flat and frontal: the downlights on the back wall are decorative and nothing on the faces corresponds to them; no rim or separation from the dark wall, so it reads as a cutscene (openmic-6-held.png, all faces; openmic-1-wide.png, back wall vs crowd)

3. Wide shot is a dense, uniform block: the crowd is packed shoulder-to-shoulder with no visible chairs and two figures standing stiffly at the back wall (openmic-1-wide.png, centre block and upper left behind)
4. Back-row clipping and odd heads: a face with a dark smear across the mouth and a figure partly cut into a neighbour (openmic-3-mid.png, back row x~490 y~340 and x~330 y~360)
5. Close-up skin is smooth and evenly lit with glassy eyes; the expression reads as a neutral smile placeholder rather than a reaction (openmic-4-face.png, centre face)
